clue.text: Opportunity to speak about rising tide causing great sadness

indicators.note: the hearing is put around the other piece, as about means surrounding

parts.note: a hearing is a chance to put one's case
a trend is a tide of opinion or fashion that is growing

explanation.surface: Someone given a chance to speak about the rising tide that is bringing great sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartrending wrings the heart, so it causes deep grief or distress.

clue.text: Rodent seen in raging stream behind hotel

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the hotel letter, sitting behind it

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a raging stream churns wildly, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A small animal glimpsed in a torrent flowing behind a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small burrowing rodent often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Sound coming from car, old

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

explanation.surface: A noise coming from an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means relating to sound, or sound itself as recorded or broadcast.

clue.text: Indian-born novelist seen in cutter in Scottish river

indicators.note: the cutter is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
a hacker is one who hacks, or cuts roughly

explanation.surface: A writer born in India spotted in a boat on a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a boat, but here it is one who hacks.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray, author of Vanity Fair, was born in Calcutta.

clue.text: Public school board fired head

indicators.note: the first letter is sacked, as an employee might be fired from the top job

parts.note: to board a bus or train is to get on it

explanation.surface: A school's governing board sacks its headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a noun for governors; it is the verb, to get on.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous fee-paying English school, which the British call a public school.

clue.text: Stylish young socialite attending very happily

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the two pieces stand together side by side

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering society
walking on air means feeling very happy

explanation.surface: A fashionable young debutante present at a party and very cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, charming and well-dressed manner.

clue.text: Beautiful young woman from New York on speed

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman from New York in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth a nymph is a beautiful maiden spirit, hence any lovely young woman.

clue.text: Check on painter, a member of a working-class movement

definitions.text: a member of a working-class movement

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A check carried out on a painter who belongs to a workers' movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a British working-class movement of the 1830s-40s demanding votes for all men.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chartist supported the People's Charter, a nineteenth-century British reform campaign.

clue.text: Bowled in an international under the most favourable conditions

parts.note: an gives the article A

indicators.note: the bowled letter is placed inside the international match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A batsman bowled out in an international match, under the best of circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: At best means taking the most optimistic view of a situation.

clue.text: Earned plenty but prepared to strike forcefully?

definitions.meaning: to make a bomb is British slang for earning a great deal of money
literally, assembled an explosive device for a powerful attack

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both slang for getting rich and literally building an explosive.

clue.text: A myth? Awful nonsense

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a myth as dreadful rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an old-fashioned expression of disbelief, like saying rubbish!

clue.text: Turn of skill, seizing lout in horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: the turned word grabs hold of the other piece, enclosing it
a turn reverses the word for skill so it reads backwards

parts.note: art is skill or craft
an oik is British slang for an uncouth lout

explanation.surface: A display of skill as a hooligan is grabbed in a carriage pulled by horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian vehicle drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Commanding batting attack

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a charge is an attack

explanation.surface: A dominant batting attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in control or authority over something is to be commanding it.

clue.text: Comment about stain

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a mark is a stain

explanation.surface: A remark made about a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written comment.

clue.text: Its contents must be made from light wood

definitions.text: Its contents must be made from light wood

parts.words: Its contents must be made from light wood
parts.note: matches are made of thin wood, and they are for lighting: light is a verb as well as an adjective

explanation.definitionFit: A small box holding matches, sticks of wood made to give light.

clue.text: Whilst abroad, touring island, this contains what I want

indicators.note: the shuffled letters travel around the island, surrounding it
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: While abroad touring an island, someone keeps a list of desires.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish list is a list of things one would like to have.

clue.text: Bad luck involved bands

parts.note: something involved is complicated, or hard
lines are bands or stripes

explanation.surface: Misfortune for some bands that were involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard lines is British slang for hard luck, a sympathetic expression of commiseration.

clue.text: Plant in front of florist's always thin on the ground

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ever means always
few means scarce, thin on the ground

explanation.surface: A plant in front of a florist's shop that is always scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a daisy-like herb of the chrysanthemum family, used for headaches.

clue.text: Leader of revolt we tartly banged up

indicators.note: banged up means battered, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel chief jailed, as we sharply report.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt in England in 1381. 'Banged up' is British slang for imprisoned, fitting the rebel's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler headed the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.

clue.text: Ghost — one appearing in cape in Scotland

indicators.note: one shows up inside the name of the cape

parts.note: Cape Wrath is the north-western tip of mainland Scotland
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spectre appearing on a Scottish headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a spectral apparition of a person, a ghost.

clue.text: In favour of side dropping amateur, for the time being

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: a side drops a player, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a team is a side

explanation.surface: Supporting a team that drops its amateur player for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore, meaning temporarily.

clue.text: Fashionable dressmaker may bring out the poet in me

indicators.note: the poet goes inside the word me

parts.note: taken as written
an odist is a poet who writes odes

explanation.surface: A fashion designer may coax the poet out of me.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a maker of fashionable dresses and hats.

clue.text: Longs to nurse poorly Greek hero

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles the other

parts.note: to ache is to long for something
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior yearns to nurse the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was the greatest Greek warrior at Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Disclose awareness of large 4

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
the answer to clue 4, the public school

explanation.surface: Revealing knowledge of a big public school.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to reveal that one knows something.

clue.text: Cool about wearing tartan

indicators.note: the about letter is clothed in tartan, sitting inside it

parts.note: plaid is tartan cloth
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Staying calm while dressed in tartan.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and unruffled, keeping cool.

clue.text: Set of beliefs, note, held by Conservative party

indicators.note: the note is held inside the other two letters

parts.note: a do is a party
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A creed held by a Conservative Party gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo, Latin for I believe, is a statement of principles.

clue.text: The pair in limbo there

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Two people stuck in limbo over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Both refers to two things together, the two of a pair.

clue.text: Fish in mouth of Tigris (river abroad)

indicators.note: a river's mouth is its start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: out means abroad, away from home

explanation.surface: A fish caught at the mouth of a foreign river, the Tigris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' suggests an estuary, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Fish goes to the bottom to cross lake

indicators.note: the sinking word stretches across the lake letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a ship founders when it sinks

explanation.surface: A fish sinks to the bottom while crossing a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Flounders are flatfish, so the plural fits the definition.

clue.text: A tennis umpire should be well-informed?

definitions.text: A tennis umpire should be well-informed?

parts.words: A tennis umpire should be well-informed?
parts.note: an umpire calls out the score, and knowing the score is an idiom for being well-informed

explanation.definitionFit: To be aware of the true facts of a situation, an idiom from keeping the tally in games.
